question: The lines $\vec{r}=(\hat{i}+2\hat{j}-\hat{k})+\lambda(2\hat{i}-\hat{j}+\hat{k})$ and $\vec{r}=(3\hat{i}+\hat{j}+2\hat{k})+\mu(\hat{i}+p\hat{j}+2\hat{k})$ are coplanar. Determine the value of $p$ and hence find their point of intersection.
explanation:
Required Condition
Let $\vec{a_1}=\hat{i}+2\hat{j}-\hat{k}$, $\vec{b_1}=2\hat{i}-\hat{j}+\hat{k}$, $\vec{a_2}=3\hat{i}+\hat{j}+2\hat{k}$ and $\vec{b_2}=\hat{i}+p\hat{j}+2\hat{k}$. Two lines $\vec{r}=\vec{a_1}+\lambda\vec{b_1}$ and $\vec{r}=\vec{a_2}+\mu\vec{b_2}$ are coplanar when
$$\left(\vec{a_2}-\vec{a_1}\right)\cdot\left(\vec{b_1}\times\vec{b_2}\right)=0$$
Here,
$$\vec{a_2}-\vec{a_1}=2\hat{i}-\hat{j}+3\hat{k}$$
Also,
$$\vec{b_1}\times\vec{b_2}=\begin{vmatrix}\hat{i}&\hat{j}&\hat{k}\\2&-1&1\\1&p&2\end{vmatrix}=(-2-p)\hat{i}-3\hat{j}+(2p+1)\hat{k}$$
Therefore, the coplanarity condition gives
$$2(-2-p)+(-1)(-3)+3(2p+1)=0$$
$$-4-2p+3+6p+3=0$$
$$4p+2=0$$
Hence,
$$p=-\frac{1}{2}$$

Evaluation of the Point of Intersection
For $p=-\frac{1}{2}$, the lines become
$$\vec{r}=(\hat{i}+2\hat{j}-\hat{k})+\lambda(2\hat{i}-\hat{j}+\hat{k})$$
and
$$\vec{r}=(3\hat{i}+\hat{j}+2\hat{k})+\mu\left(\hat{i}-\frac{1}{2}\hat{j}+2\hat{k}\right)$$
Equating corresponding coordinates gives
$$1+2\lambda=3+\mu,\quad 2-\lambda=1-\frac{\mu}{2},\quad -1+\lambda=2+2\mu$$
The first equation gives $\mu=2\lambda-2$. Substituting this in the third equation,
$$-1+\lambda=2+2(2\lambda-2)$$
$$-1+\lambda=4\lambda-2$$
so $\lambda=\frac{1}{3}$ and consequently $\mu=-\frac{4}{3}$. These values also satisfy the second equation.

Substituting $\lambda=\frac{1}{3}$ in the first line gives the common point
$$\left(1+\frac{2}{3},\;2-\frac{1}{3},\;-1+\frac{1}{3}\right)=\left(\frac{5}{3},\frac{5}{3},-\frac{2}{3}\right)$$

Final Result
The required value is $p=-\frac{1}{2}$, and the coplanar lines intersect at $\left(\frac{5}{3},\frac{5}{3},-\frac{2}{3}\right)$.

options.D: $p=-\frac{1}{2}$; the lines are parallel and have no point of intersection.
